header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Carlson (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Aurora Head of Security), Priya Rao (Aurora Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Aurora IT Ops)
summary: Redwood walked through audit logging and admin activity capabilities. Customer concerned about what events are captured, export options to SIEM, retention/archival controls, encryption/KMS integration, and SSO/RBAC visibility. Agree to share detailed schema, run sample export to customer's SIEM, and confirm retention/legal hold requirements.
topics: What audit logs capture (admin, API, console, model access, prompt traces?)
Export options (S3, syslog, webhook, SIEM connectors)
Encryption and KMS integration for logs
Demo of admin activity UI and sample log line
transcript:
00:00 Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we only have 45 minutes so we'll focus on audit logs and admin activity logging for your compliance team. Marcus, can you confirm the scope you want to cover?
00:12 Marcus: yeah thanks Jamie, uh, main things are — what do you capture by default, especially admin changes, user provisioning, model version rollouts, and any prompt or input traces. Also export and retention, we have a 7-year legal hold for some payments data so we need options.
00:28 Jamie: totally, that's helpful. quick intro — i'm Jamie, AE, nina here is our se who will go into export formats and examples.
00:36 Nina: hi all, nina patel, i run security integrations. i'll show examples and we can talk SIEM ingest.
00:44 Liam: quick note, we're on AWS primarily, S3 and Splunk for logs. we want to avoid sending PII to third parties.
01:00 Nina: got it. so high level — our audit logging captures three buckets: admin console actions (user create, role changes, api key creation/revocation), API/ingest events (request metadata, model id, tokens consumed, but we redact user content by default for hosted), and system events (deploys, autoscale, infra tickets).
01:28 Marcus: when you say redact, what exactly is removed? prompts? or the full user messages?
01:34 Nina: for hosted we redact full prompt text unless customer opts into full-text logging via private deployment or explicit config. we surface metadata like request id, model, token counts, timestamp, user id hash, and policy flags.
01:52 Marcus: okay we need that documented for SOC2 and our auditors.
01:58 Jamie: we'll attach the schema. nina, can you mention export options?
02:05 Nina: sure. you can stream logs to customer S3 buckets (preferred for retention/ingest), to a syslog endpoint, or push to SIEM via a connector (we have tested with Splunk/Datadog — though third-party names may be slightly off in the transcript), or webhook delivery. Exports can be configured at account or org level, and you can apply filters (only admin logs, only console events, etc).
02:32 Priya: if we use S3 export, are logs encrypted at rest with our KMS? we require customer-managed keys.
02:38 Nina: yes, S3 exports can be encrypted with customer KMS keys; for private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. For hosted S3 delivery we support SSE-KMS with your key arn.
02:52 Liam: how about integrity and immutability? legal wants immutable retention and proofs of tamper. any WORM or object lock support?
03:02 Nina: S3 object lock is supported if you use your own bucket; retention policies can be enforced on your side. Redwood's internal retention can also be configured but for legal hold we recommend customer bucket with object lock enabled.
03:18 Marcus: what about admin activity in the console — do you capture old/new values for role changes?
03:24 Nina: yes we capture event type, actor id, actor IP, scope, target resource, and a diff of changed fields where applicable. diffs are limited in size to avoid leaking big blobs.
03:38 Marcus: good. question on model access — do you log token-level metadata and KV cache access?
03:44 Nina: we log model id, sequence length, token counts, latency, and cache hit/miss metrics. we do not log KV cache contents. sometimes terms get munged in the transcription — K-V cache contents are not logged.
04:00 Priya: auditors might ask for correlation ids to link an API request to a user session. do you provide request ids?
04:06 Nina: yes every request has a request_id and trace id. you can also enable trace headers.
04:12 Liam: how long do logs live by default in hosted mode?
04:16 Jamie: default retention is 90 days for hosted logs, but exports to customer S3 are recommended for longer retention. for dedicated/private we can configure longer retention.
04:28 Marcus: 90 days won't work for our 7-year requirement. so we'll need S3 export and lifecycle to glacier or long-term cold storage.
04:36 Nina: yep that's the common pattern — export daily to S3, lifecycle rules to GLACIER or Glacier Deep Archive.
04:44 Jamie: note on data residency — if you have EU customers we can export to EU buckets and we have region routing.
04:52 Marcus: we have EU customers too, yes. encryption in transit?
04:56 Nina: TLS 1.2+ in transit, and if you use webhook or syslog we support mTLS where possible.
05:04 Priya: what about RBAC auditing — like who changed IAM roles in your platform versus SSO events?
05:12 Nina: we capture SSO events (SAML/SAML responses sometimes show up as samel in logs) — sorry, transcription aside — we log SSO provider events (login, logout, token refresh) and mapping to platform roles. RBAC changes are admin events.
05:30 Marcus: do you integrate with our IDP for real-time provisioning?
05:34 Jamie: yes we support SCIM provisioning and can sync groups; SCIM events are logged too.
05:40 Liam: can we get a demo of a single admin change in the UI and then the raw log line?
05:46 Nina: sure, i'll share a quick snippet then. (screen share) 05:55 Nina: here's the admin audit UI — shows actor, timestamp, action, and the diff. raw log sample: {event_type: "admin.change", timestamp: "2026-03-04T14:23:10Z", actor_id: "u-8234", actor_email: "mlee@aurora.com", resource: "role:operator", changes: ["add: role:payments-review"] , request_id: "req-9ab3"} — note sample shows redactable fields, and in actual exports keys are normalized to snake_case.
07:10 Marcus: that sample helps. can you include sample lines that show redacted prompt content?
07:16 Nina: yes — for hosted we show something like {event_type: "api.request", model_id: "rwd-bert-13b", request_id: "req-", user_hash: "ha_...", tokens: 132, prompt_redacted: true} and if you opt-in for full logs the prompt_text field appears.
07:40 Marcus: are logs signed or otherwise verifiable?
07:44 Nina: we support signing exports if you want; we can add a signature manifest per daily export. that's part of the enterprise package.
07:52 Liam: about SIEM, we use Splunk — do you have a certified app or should we ingest via S3?
07:58 Nina: ingestion via S3 is simplest; we have sample Splunk SPL to pull and parse the JSON. for realtime you can pipe to syslog or webhook. we've done Splunk and Datadog integrations in the past.
08:12 Marcus: any PII concerns — are user emails stored in logs?
08:16 Nina: we store user identifiers; email can be included but we recommend hashing or pseudonymizing. you can opt for user_id_hash only.
08:26 Marcus: auditors will ask about access controls to logs — who at Redwood can see customer logs?
08:32 Jamie: access is limited to authorized support/ops with RBAC; access is logged and requires Jira ticket approval for elevated access. we'll share our SOC2 control for support access protocol.
08:48 Priya: do you keep an access log for when Redwood personnel view customer logs?
08:52 Jamie: yes we have an audit trail for internal access and will provide sample reports.
09:00 Marcus: do you have an API to pull logs programmatically?
09:04 Nina: yes, we have a logs export API and you can also configure push to S3. API access is authenticated with client credentials and supports pagination.
09:14 Marcus: what's the max retention you can configure on-prem/private?
09:18 Jamie: in private deployments you control retention entirely; in dedicated we can negotiate retention up to multi-year as part of contract. hosted has practical limits due to storage costs but export to client bucket avoids that.
09:32 Marcus: two more small things — can you preserve raw request bodies for a short window for debugging while keeping them redacted for longer term?
09:40 Nina: yes we support tiered retention: raw request bodies kept for X days (configurable) then purged or replaced with redacted forms.
09:48 Liam: ok let's talk timeline — we want PoC to validate Splunk ingest and object lock by mid-march.
09:56 Jamie: action items — i'll send the schema and SOC2 docs by Friday; nina will run sample export and share instructions; marcus will confirm retention policy specifics. any objections?
10:12 Marcus: no objections, sounds good. thanks everyone.
10:18 Jamie: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed PoC schedule.
10:24 [meeting ends]
